## Computation of $H_n(M-\{p\};\mathbb{Z})$

**Setup.** Let $M$ be a closed, oriented, connected $n$-manifold and $p\in M$. Consider the long exact sequence of the pair $(M, M-\{p\})$:

$$\cdots \to H_{n+1}(M,M-\{p\}) \to H_n(M-\{p\}) \xrightarrow{i_*} H_n(M) \xrightarrow{j_*} H_n(M,M-\{p\}) \xrightarrow{\partial} H_{n-1}(M-\{p\}) \to H_{n-1}(M) \to \cdots$$

**Step 1 — Identify the relative groups via excision.** Choose a coordinate ball $U\cong \mathbb{R}^n$ around $p$ with $U\subseteq M$ open. By excision of $M-\{p\}$ from the complement of $U$,

$$H_k(M, M-\{p\}) \cong H_k(U, U-\{p\}).$$

Since $U\cong\mathbb{R}^n$ and $U-\{p\}\cong\mathbb{R}^n-\{0\}\simeq S^{n-1}$, the long exact sequence of the pair $(U,U-\{p\})$ together with $H_k(U)=0$ for $k>0$ gives

$$H_k(U, U-\{p\}) \cong \widetilde{H}_{k-1}(S^{n-1}) \cong \begin{cases} \mathbb{Z}, & k=n,\\ 0, & k\neq n.\end{cases}$$

Hence

$$H_k(M, M-\{p\};\mathbb{Z}) \cong \begin{cases}\mathbb{Z}, & k=n,\\ 0, & k\neq n.\end{cases}$$

In particular $H_{n+1}(M,M-\{p\})=0$.

**Step 2 — Identify the absolute group.** Since $M$ is closed, oriented, and connected, $H_n(M;\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}$, generated by the fundamental class $[M]$.

**Step 3 — The map $j_*$ is an isomorphism.** Under the excision isomorphism $H_n(M,M-\{p\})\cong H_n(U,U-\{p\})\cong\mathbb{Z}$, the map $j_*:H_n(M)\to H_n(M,M-\{p\})$ corresponds to the restriction of the fundamental class to the local pair $(U,U-\{p\})$. By the local-to-global characterization of the fundamental class of an oriented manifold, $[M]$ restricts to a generator of $H_n(U,U-\{p\})\cong\mathbb{Z}$ at every point $p$. (Equivalently: the orientation of $M$ is a consistent choice of local generators, and $[M]$ is the unique global class whose local restriction at each $p$ is the chosen local generator.) Therefore $j_*$ sends the generator $[M]$ to a generator, so

$$j_*: H_n(M)\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} H_n(M,M-\{p\})$$

is an isomorphism.

**Step 4 — Conclude via exactness.** From the segment

$$0 = H_{n+1}(M,M-\{p\}) \to H_n(M-\{p\}) \xrightarrow{i_*} H_n(M) \xrightarrow{j_*}_{\sim} H_n(M,M-\{p\}),$$

exactness gives $\ker j_* = \operatorname{im} i_*$, and since $j_*$ is an isomorphism, $\ker j_*=0$. Also $i_*$ is injective (its kernel equals $\operatorname{im} H_{n+1}(M,M-\{p\})=0$). Thus $i_*$ is an injection with image $\ker j_*=0$, forcing

$$H_n(M-\{p\};\mathbb{Z}) = 0.$$

**Consistency check.** For $n\geq 2$, $M-\{p\}$ is a connected noncompact $n$-manifold, and a noncompact $n$-manifold has trivial top homology — consistent with the result. For $n=1$, $M\cong S^1$ and $M-\{p\}\cong\mathbb{R}$ is contractible, so $H_1=0$ — also consistent.

---

**Answer.**

$$\boxed{\,H_n\!\bigl(M-\{p\};\mathbb{Z}\bigr)\cong 0\,}$$

The key point is that for a closed oriented connected $n$-manifold, the fundamental class $[M]\in H_n(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ maps isomorphically onto the local homology $H_n(M,M-\{p\})\cong\mathbb{Z}$ at every point $p$; exactness of the pair sequence then forces $H_n(M-\{p\})=0$.
